beats.narration_text: Scout is a Slack agent that reads my resume and then goes looking for jobs I could actually get. It worked. But working and production ready are two different claims, and this week I went after the gap between them. This is Sai. Five correctness bugs, a restructure onto two interfaces, a hundred and seventy tests, and a container. The bug I want to show you was the quietest one, because the code had been compensating for it the whole time.

1 of them was hidden by a defensive cast

beats.narration_text: Scout's reach is a pile of small modules. Six job sources, each one file with a register function, each hitting the employer's own public endpoint rather than scraping it. Greenhouse alone serves eight companies off one board API. Google is the exception, with no API at all. The model never learns any of this. It reads the schemas the registry builds, and picks.

show.event: Spark line sets up the tool surface
Six source chips land one at a time, dot filling as each settles
Caption names the shared contract underneath them

props.sparkLine: Six job sources, one tool contract
props.caption: Each source is one module with a register() function. Adding one is a file, not a refactor.

beats.narration_text: Here's the one worth your time. The registry turns a Python function into a schema by reading its annotations. But every module in Scout starts with from future import annotations, so an annotation isn't a type any more. It's the string, quote, int. The type map never matched, so the model was told days and limit were strings. It never looked broken, because both functions cast to int on the way in.

Track A peels off: annotation read straight off the signature
Track A's block lands warn-toned — the model is told 'string'
Track B runs the rail: get_type_hints resolves the real type
Track B's block lands good-toned — schema says integer

tracks.label: get_type_hints()
notes: String resolved to a real type

beats.narration_text: Then the deployment question, which turned out to be a fork I couldn't think my way around. Scout runs in Socket Mode: it holds an outbound websocket to Slack and listens on no port. So scale-to-zero isn't a config change. Slack can't wake a stopped process, because there's no address to reach it at. I shipped the always-on worker and wrote the other path down.

show.event: The question card sets the fork
Spine draws down; first elbow reaches the always-on card
Second elbow reaches the scale-to-zero card, warn-toned
Ghost line surfaces the 3-second ack trap
Resolver lands terracotta — what actually shipped

data.question: How does a Socket Mode bot stay reachable?

branches.label: Stay running
branches.detail: Holds a websocket. Listens on no port.
branches.fix: ECS Fargate, or a GCE e2-micro

branches.label: Scale to zero
branches.detail: No address for Slack to reach.

resolver.label: Shipped the worker
resolver.detail: Dockerfile plus SIGTERM handling. Ping-to-wake is documented, not built.

data.ghostText: Ping-to-wake must also ack within 3 seconds, or Slack retries three times.

beats.narration_text: So what the week actually bought. Two interfaces did most of the work: a chat backend that normalizes one provider, and a conversational agent interface the Slack layer talks to. Once those existed the restructure stopped being risky, because the seams were named. Working and production ready are different claims, and the distance between them is mostly things your code is already apologizing for.

show.event: Artifact panel opens on the cream ground
Four numbered recap lines land in sequence

artifactLines: A defensive int() cast was hiding a real type bug from the model.
Two interfaces, ChatBackend and ConversationalAgent, made the restructure cheap.
170 tests run in 0.26 seconds with no network and no credentials.
It ships as a container. Ping-to-wake is written down, not built.

beats.narration_text: Your turn, and this one is worth running on your own code. Paste this: find every place my code defends against a value it should never have received, and tell me what upstream bug that defence is hiding. That is the shape of the whole thing. A cast, a default, a try except that quietly makes bad input work. Each one is a place where something upstream is already wrong and you have stopped being able to see it.
